heading: Power laws extend beyond text pretraining under specific conditions
definition: the same power-law form holds in other modalities and training regimes (e.g. image and video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer).
summary: Several independent groups find power-law regions in image, speech and fine-tuning studies, but an unchanged law across modalities and training regimes is contested. Repeated data can worsen validation loss, and increasing adapter capacity can bring negligible improvements or worsen performance.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: C for unrestricted extension, R2 for conditional power-law regions; 1-10B: C for unrestricted extension, R2 for conditional regions; 10-100B: R2 for task-specific fine-tuning laws, with unchanged-form generality unresolved; >100B: ?.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to the unrestricted 'same power-law form' wording. Independent conditional extensions support R2: mixed-modal image and speech losses fit additive parameter/data laws (arXiv:2301.03728#R2, arXiv:2301.03728#R3, arXiv:2301.03728#R6), and bilingual fine-tuning fits task-specific joint laws over 1B–16B (arXiv:2402.17193#r3, arXiv:2402.17193#r5). However, jointly tuned repeated-data parameter scaling can follow a power law while fixed-size loss increases with additional epochs (arXiv:2509.14786#R3, arXiv:2509.14786#R1). Default weight decay gives no significant parameter-scaling improvement, and weight decay transferred from 150M gives non-monotone scaling; these conditions challenge V5. Transferring epoch count produces earlier saturation, a separate limits_scope condition (arXiv:2509.14786#R8). Qwen3 SFT supports saturating size laws over 0.6B–32B, but repeated-pass 8B training raises validation NLL (arXiv:2609.01244#R1, arXiv:2609.01244#R7, arXiv:2609.01244#R14). The Llama offset against the Qwen3 fit does not test a separate Llama power-law form and supplies no V5 verdict (arXiv:2609.01244#R9). Fresh-example gains are local interaction checks without a fitted data law and supply no V5 support (arXiv:2609.01244#R10, arXiv:2609.01244#R11). Bilingual adapter-capacity scaling can also be negligible or inverse (arXiv:2402.17193#r21, arXiv:2402.17193#r22). Relevant coverage keys are versions.V5.verdicts, versions.V5.studies_by_size and versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size; these unreconciled pre-check summaries cannot establish corrected verdict totals, missing evidence or replication quality. The checked classifications above govern this status: arXiv:2509.14786#R8 is excluded from support and split between challenges for default or transferred weight decay and limits_scope for transferred epoch count; arXiv:2609.01244#R9 is excluded from V5 limits and arXiv:2609.01244#R10 and arXiv:2609.01244#R11 from V5 support because they do not test its power-law form. Regenerated counts and coverage gaps remain pending a traceable reconciliation of checked classifications, exclusions and relocations; no corrected totals or missing-evidence claims are inferred from the unreconciled summaries.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent held-out comparisons using a prespecified common formula, matched objectives, separate unique-data and repetition axes, and per-size optimization would clarify whether failures persist under comparable conditions. Such comparisons could establish a narrower R2 claim. Independently validated loss-law tests above 100B would resolve that scale's status.

Repeated supervised fine-tuning raised validation loss after about two epochs.
Larger recommendation language models had worse out-of-distribution perplexity under repeated-data training.
EEGNeX showed no apparent data scaling on ISRUC.
Wider single-layer physics-informed neural networks often increased error or showed no significant benefit.
Exponential fits outperformed power laws in tested quadratic and ReLU modular-addition networks.
Roll Ball success remained low and failed to improve predictably with more data.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A controlled video-generative loss law separating unique-data quantity from repetition amount, including sustained high-reuse training.
untested.basis: The supplied packs do not identify this joint test. arXiv:2411.17470#r1 uses total training tokens T = BS on Panda-70M without separate unique-data and repetition variables or a controlled reuse experiment; no explicit exclusion of repetition is reported. arXiv:2607.28611#R2 uses sub-epoch runs; arXiv:2608.28404#r12 fits exposure through approximately 4.5 epochs and lists later repetition as point losses without a fitted law; arXiv:2610.12464#R1 measures fidelity with data and steps coupled. Counts keys versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.scaling and versions.V5.studies_by_stage record broad scaling coverage but do not distinguish unique video data from reuse.

untested.what: Separate modality-specific loss laws within the supplied tri-modal masked-diffusion setup.
untested.basis: arXiv:2602.21472#R1 fits pooled text, image-text and audio-text ELBO in Section 5.3 and Figure 11; no separate modality-specific scaling laws within that tri-modal setup are reported. Appendix E reports a separate text-only MDM sweep, and Section 7.2 reports modality-mixture ablations. Other packs supply modality-specific multimodal MoE fits, including arXiv:2610.14423#r2 and arXiv:2610.14423#r3, but these use a different model and objective. Counts keys versions.V5.main_rows_by_operation and versions.V5.studies_by_family do not resolve this objective-specific gap.

untested.what: Whether end-to-end SGD/GD training attains the stated hierarchical multi-index data-scaling rates.
untested.basis: arXiv:2602.05846 explicitly leaves end-to-end gradient training open. Its network result, arXiv:2602.05846#R6, uses spectral initialization followed by ridge readout; #R5 and #R7 concern spectral estimation. No supplied partial establishes the missing training procedure for this target family. Counts key versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.training does not distinguish these algorithms.

wording_issues.issue: Power-law components can persist while the joint expression changes. Distillation adds teacher cross-entropy and a broken factor depending on teacher loss relative to the student's supervised-equivalent loss; fixing the teacher does not remove student-size and token dependence. Symbolic music adds parameter–data interactions and transformed effective data, with accurate predictions before early stopping. Dense-to-MoE upcycling shows conditional power-law scaling with coupled training-stage budgets. Repeated-data retrieval favors multiplicative parameter–unique-data terms over additive pretraining forms. These results do not establish one unchanged joint formula.

A response linear in log resource is a different fitted form. BUTTER uses powers of log parameter count; HSTU fits a+b ln C; EgoScale fits action MSE linear in ln data; UniWAM also fits loss linear in ln data hours. Such relationships do not establish a power law in the measured response.

The phrase combines parameter scaling under a fixed corpus, unique-data scaling, presented-token scaling and loss along additional epochs. Joint tuning can recover monotone parameter scaling; default weight decay gives no significant improvement, transferred weight decay gives non-monotone scaling, and transferred epoch count gives earlier saturation. Fixed-size epoch curves can worsen. Replay order changes loss at matched counts but does not determine whether either order follows a power law. Repeated force-field training shows early power-law behavior that breaks during later repetition. Successful stopped-minimum fits do not imply continued improvement with repetition.

Pretrained size, fine-tuning data, trainable rank and training duration are different scaling axes. Pythia off-task WikiText2 loss fits depend on SFT learning rate, with explicit OpenAI-law breakdown for GSM8K at the higher rate. Bilingual PET trainable-parameter effects can be negligible or inverse. Astraios Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA initially show increasing loss with model size, with recovery under separate learning-rate retuning; the initial Prompt Tuning rate is not unambiguously specified. Decreasing loss under the main Astraios settings does not establish a power-law form. A VLM law fitting within Falcon3 does not give a unified parameter-count curve across Falcon3 and Llama-3.2; that cross-family mismatch alone does not establish form failure.

Transfer fits are conditional on source–target relationship, data regime and evaluation distribution. The Python effective-transfer power law ceases to fit well outside its low-data region, at DF/D(N) > 0.10. Materials transfer shows almost no or no improvement in some polymer classes and non-WF compounds; the polymer-class evidence is tentative because samples are small, and weak physical relatedness is not established as its sole explanation. Pythia cat-genome transfer is erratic. Gameplay continual pretraining raises loss on unseen worlds; in-corpus loss improves under diverse mixtures S2–S5 but rises under Minecraft-only S1 training.

The dependent quantities differ. Image diffusion FID scales more cleanly than validation NLL on the combined scaling curve across model sizes; these are aggregate findings, not separately established laws for an individual model. Audio evidence can concern downstream HEAR scores and support power-law-plus-constant forms; saturation alone does not contradict those forms. EHR optimal parameter/token allocation fits do not test V5's loss form. Intrinsic RL performance constructs a power-law compute frontier by definition. The measured quantity must be specified before treating these as evidence for a held-out pretraining-loss law.

A constant exponent need not describe the full range. RoboJEPA benefits from logarithmic curvature; long-context continual pretraining needs a negative finite-range offset; materials data curves use broken laws; mathematical GRPO has S-shaped full trajectories with vanishing local slopes at its extremes. Exponent disagreement alone also does not reject the existence of a power-law region.

An unrestricted decreasing-loss interpretation includes tested exceptions. Modular-addition networks, including two-layer ReLU networks, favor floor exponentials over floor power laws. Standard-capacity Roll Ball has no predictable data improvement, whereas increased denoiser capacity restores it. PINN error can increase with width. Quadratic-network theory has a noisy under-regularized overfitting phase with increasing error and a rank-collapse regime with constant leading-order error; these challenge decreasing-error scaling in their named conditions.

Directional improvements, qualitative author descriptions and high fit scores for unspecified functions do not identify a power law. BOTANIC-0 reports improving loss without establishing a power-law form. Microbiome models report decreasing loss described as linear in logarithmic model size, without a power-law fit or exponent. PointWorld supplies sparse tabulated capacity comparisons and a qualitative log-linear trend; diminishing absolute gains do not establish a failed power law. STELLAR reports improving loss with flattening curves while qualifying strong LLM-like scaling. Evidence with changing data and model size together also does not isolate either scaling axis.

The modality label does not specify the tested objective or initialization. UCF101 single-image classification does not test temporal modeling. MM-DiT's preliminary video trend starts from pretrained image weights and shows smooth validation-loss decreases without a power-law fit or exponent; V5's form remains untested there. HunyuanVideo reports allocation fits rather than direct loss exponents. Native image–text training can mask vision tokens and fit text-token loss.

method_sensitivity.what: Joint per-size tuning restores repeated-data parameter scaling. Default weight decay gives no significant improvement, transferred weight decay gives non-monotone scaling, and transferred epoch counts give earlier saturation; sufficiently high epoch counts reverse improvement. Matched CommonCrawl repetition counts differ with order: consecutive replay adds up to 0.46 bpb relative to spaced presentation, without testing power-law form under either order. Repeated UR50/S severely overfits protein MLM, while the 3B CLM has diminishing returns. Repeated-data JetClass retains power-law dataset scaling under early stopping; across dataset sizes above the threshold, its repeated-data trajectory retains the compute exponent but requires roughly 10× more compute for comparable loss. Fixed-dataset compute curves can saturate or overfit.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, schedule and convergence filtering
method_sensitivity.what: Astraios StarCoder 1B–3B Prompt Tuning/AdaLoRA loss initially increases with model size and decreases after learning-rate retuning. The initial Prompt Tuning rate is ambiguous; recovery establishes neither a power-law form nor exponent or allocation dependence. Pythia off-task WikiText2 scaling fits deteriorate at higher SFT learning rates, including OpenAI-law GSM8K R²=0.0000 at 2e-4. Oracle-learning-rate refitting changes the Qwen3 FullFT size exponent from 0.51 to 0.33. ScaleMAE's data-fit R² is 0.941 after retaining trials that surpassed the local minimum and excluding trapped trials, versus 0.18 with all trials. Thus optimization and run selection change both apparent scaling and fit quality.

method_sensitivity.factor: Functional form, offsets, estimator and fitting interval
method_sensitivity.what: RoboJEPA curved fits with a compute-dependent exponent extrapolate more accurately than constant-exponent fits on DROID and RoboCasa holdouts; this qualifies V5's same-form claim. Data-constrained retrieval favors multiplicative parameter×unique-data terms over additive pretraining forms. Long-context CPT requires a negative free offset, approximately −0.6 to −0.8; zero/nonnegative-offset alternatives give S5 R²=−0.10 and −4.09, and the authors describe a finite-range law. ScaleRL asymptote predictions change with the compute interval; only its high-compute fit recovers observed saturation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Measured loss, calibration and error aggregation
method_sensitivity.what: For VGG on CIFAR-10/100, non-calibrated NLL at temperature 1 shows double descent and cannot be approximated by a power law over the considered sizes; temperature-calibrated single-network NLL admits a close power-law fit. For EDM2 at log σ=4.38 on ImageNet-64, subtracting optimal loss improves envelope correlation from 0.82 to 0.94. T5 cross-entropy scaling persists where en–fr BLEU breaks with 100% en-MC4; the BLEU failure concerns V6. KAN [2,1,1] grid scaling retains a power-law form under both aggregations: roughly G^-3 for mean-based RMSE and closer to G^-4 for median-based error. Aggregation changes the exponent without limiting V5's form claim.

method_sensitivity.factor: Scaled component, architecture and resource balance
method_sensitivity.what: Graph SSL can improve with depth while showing no consistent gain from width at fixed depth. Bilingual fine-tuning distinguishes useful pretrained-size scaling from negligible or inverse PET-capacity scaling. Phi3-3B test CE rises 0.018→0.251→0.602 as LoRA rank increases 32→128→512; accuracy is 0.856 at ranks 32 and 128, then 0.864 at rank 512. TSP width-scaling fits at fixed D=6,12,24,42 use W=128,256,512; depth-scaling fits at fixed W=128,256,512 use D=6,12,24,42. These component-specific fits are tighter than the pooled parameter-only law, whose R²=0.794. Nominal parameter growth therefore does not specify an interchangeable intervention.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data quality, sampling, diversity and construction
method_sensitivity.what: Gait filtering changes the fitted data exponent from 0.078 to 0.132. Wearable IMU fold-0 exponents differ between USER sampling, −0.049, and RANDOM sampling, −0.017. New teacher-generated math problems support declining-error fits, whereas additional self-generated solutions to fixed questions can plateau or worsen. Single-cell validation trajectories depend on proportional versus uniform cell-type sampling. Data quantity therefore changes together with consequential aspects of content and coverage.

method_sensitivity.factor: Source–target relationship, evaluation domain and horizon
method_sensitivity.what: Gameplay continual pretraining lowers in-corpus loss under diverse mixtures S2–S5; Minecraft-only S1 raises it. OOD loss ends higher at 1,600 h than at 50 h. Stereo in-domain power-law segments do not carry over to zero-shot cross-domain EPE, which can stop improving or worsen. Swin weather data-scaling fits deteriorate for low-level meridional wind past approximately 180 h. Global R² reaches a trough near 190–200 h; the compute exponent is closer to zero at 240 h than at 6 h, and long-lead compute fits have channel-specific low-R² pockets. WorldPM improves more favorably on adversarial tests than on subjective tests, whose loss does not decrease with more preference data. These comparisons change the evaluated distribution, target or forecast horizon.

Raw HuBERT speech tokens have parameter/data exponents 0.25/0.24 versus 0.15/0.16 after unigram compression. On DL3DV with VC=4, vanilla multiview SVSM initially improves but saturates and stops scaling much earlier than LVSM; PRoPE restores scaling. Including visual-encoder compute changes the encoder-based multimodal loss exponent from 0.300 to 0.362. Order-book scaling weakens when measured latency replaces structural work, with latency-fit R²=0.468. Tokenization, conditioning and the resource coordinate affect the measured relation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task structure, dropout, labels, spectra and learning dynamics
method_sensitivity.what: Empirical supervised MNIST FCNN experiments independently vary training and evaluation neuron dropout; data-scaling exponents become negative, positive or approximately zero across phases. On fixed whitened ViT features, teacher labels expose approximate one-third scaling while real labels reach a floor earlier. Context-updated nonlinear attention retains depth scaling for top-2 aggregation but shows no improvement with depth for top-16. PLRF regression compute exponents depend on feature/target decay and optimizer or schedule. Phase Aa additionally requires α+β>0.5. The scheduled Aa⋆ risk result is an achievable upper bound, not a matching risk characterization.

method_sensitivity.factor: RL task complexity, objective, diversity and batch selection
method_sensitivity.what: Single-agent RL fits exclude an early transient; intrinsic performance makes its compute frontier a power law by construction. AdA size gains reverse on an empty-room task distribution, with teacher differences complicating the comparison. BRO allocation fits vary by task and become unstable with borrowed fixed-batch data; h1-crawl optima are reported unpredictable despite at least 50 seeds per setting. Agentic RL needs an environment×task interaction, improving R² from 0.93 to 0.98; content-only environment variation gives exponent 0.07 versus 0.41 for the default pool.
